prompt: Explore int overflow: complete sumAsInt, which adds two ints and may wrap around, and sumAsLong, which must widen to long BEFORE adding so the true sum survives.
explanation: An int holds 32 bits, so Integer.MAX_VALUE + 1 silently wraps around to Integer.MIN_VALUE -- Java does not throw an error on overflow. Writing (long) a + b widens a to 64 bits first, which forces the addition itself to happen in long arithmetic, so the true sum fits. Writing (long) (a + b) instead casts after the int addition has already overflowed, which preserves the wrong wrapped value.
hints: sumAsInt is just a + b; the interesting part is watching what the tests say it does at Integer.MAX_VALUE.
In sumAsLong, cast one operand: (long) a + b. That makes the + itself a long addition.
(long) (a + b) does NOT work: the ints are added (and wrap) before the cast is applied.
